correctness.rationale: Funk–Hecke and the Gegenbauer differential identity give the cap multipliers, with m_1 positive and m_2=m_1 cos(r). The two-cap operator is the product of commuting scalar-on-harmonics operators, so B_(r,s) is symmetric and the mixture spectrum is the quadratic form of M on the multiplier pair. Continuity and absolute summability of the spherical expansion (by the Hilbert–Schmidt cap identities and Cauchy–Schwarz) justify the finite-Gram equivalence. The two conjugate generating-function singularities give the stated positive leading amplitudes and a normalized O(1/l) error. Rational independence gives Weyl equidistribution separately on l=2j and l=2j+1. The zero set of the limiting nonzero trigonometric polynomial has area zero, so the small error does not change the relative sign density on either subsequence. A negative direction intersects the interior of the rectangle of attainable phase pairs; the preimage has positive area. For a nonzero PSD M the same reasoning supplies infinitely many strictly positive degrees of both parities, enough for strict positivity. Complementary multipliers satisfy m_l(pi-r)=(-1)^(l+1)m_l(r) for l>0 and the constant term is checked separately. Both parity factors are necessary by m_1 and m_2; if strict, the Gegenbauer recurrence at cos(r) != 0 forbids successive same-parity zeros and gives strict positivity. Equality kills all positive degrees of one parity, with a possible constant term insufficient for strictness. The indefinite example satisfies the exact inequalities. The supplied CHECK.py was inspected, not run. The independent S^3 sine-integral test in python /workspace/reproductions/reproduce.py gave negative even/odd fractions .599420/.599480 versus phase area .59954860, and verified the complementary identity numerically. The proof, not this finite sample, establishes the all-degree claims.

value.rationale: The result determines when a natural signed two-scale covariance kernel remains positive semidefinite, gives a quantitative spectral obstruction in the generic case, and exhibits an exact contrasting cone where an indefinite coefficient matrix is possible. The strictness test separates positive spectra supported in only one parity from finite-set strict positivity. It is not a classification for other arithmetic resonances or for the circle.
